transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve just felt very shut down lately. Like the part of me that used to want to reach out to people, or enjoy my work, yoga, galleries, even journaling… it’s gone kind of quiet. I’m mostly just getting through what I have to do.
How long have you been feeling this way — has it been a few weeks, or more like months or years?
More like months. I think… about eight months now. It started after we took my older relative into our apartment, and since then things have just felt different.
Have you ever had a stretch of days or weeks where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it didn't last long?
Not really. I don’t think I’ve had anything like that… if anything, I’ve felt more slowed down.

Besides feeling shut down and losing interest in things, have you noticed changes in your sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, or feelings of guilt or worthlessness during these past eight months?

I’m not sure. I mean… sleep maybe isn’t perfect, but I haven’t really been tracking it. Appetite seems about the same, I think. Concentration is a little hard to judge. I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around feeling worthless or anything… it’s more just flat, I guess.
Before your relative moved in about eight months ago, would you say you generally felt like your usual self — with normal energy and interest in things — most of the time?
Yes… before that, I think I was mostly myself. The change has really been these last eight months, since my relative moved in — in how I’m thinking, working, and being with people.
Would you say this low, shut-down feeling is with you nearly every day, most of the day, or does it come and go depending on what's happening with your relative or other circumstances?

It’s… pretty much there most days. Maybe it shifts a little depending on what’s happening at home, but it’s not just that.

It’s like the part of me that used to reach out to people, or enjoy work, yoga, galleries, even writing in my journal… it’s gone quiet. I mostly just get through what I have to do.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed yourself having trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than you used to?
I don’t know… not in a clear way. Some nights are off, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been sleeping much more. I haven’t really kept track.
Even when you get a break from caregiving duties or your relative isn't around, do you still feel that same flat, shut-down mood, or does it lift somewhat?

It doesn’t really lift much. Even when I have space, I still feel… kind of flat.

The things I used to naturally reach for — people, work, yoga, going to galleries, writing — they just don’t pull me in the same way. I mostly just do what has to be done.
Have you been having any thoughts of guilt, feeling like you're a burden, or feeling worthless during this time?

I don’t think so… not really in that way.

I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been sitting around feeling worthless or like a burden.

This represents a clear change from previous baseline functioning. No manic/hypomanic symptoms were elicited, ruling out bipolar spectrum. Adjustment disorder with depressed mood was considered given the temporal link to caregiving stress, but the pervasive, non-reactive nature and depth of anhedonia lasting 8 months exceeds typical adjustment-related presentations, favoring a depressive episode diagnosis.
